Swedbank's own IR consensus is dated 15 Oct, before Handelsbanken reported, and still asks the most aggressive q/q NII step of the three banks (+4.1%) after both peers missed on funding costs; the stock fell only 0.95% on Handelsbanken's day. It is a peer-derived hypothesis rather than a company document, with real offsets (Baltic ECB pass-through, weaker SEK, extra day) and a Pillar 1 disclosure that could land either way, so the size stays modest on a name whose median report-day move is ~1.1%.

The Delaware Supreme Court's 24 Sep reversal in Gendreau v. Movora is the genuinely unpriced item - no issuer release, no Swedish coverage, flat tape on the day - but it is a one-off worth only ~0.5% of market cap with a remand and collection risk, so it barely offsets a segment build that puts organic growth 0.5-1pp under the 7.58% bar as Specialty Pharma laps the US campaign; Fidelio's SEK 390m of pre-closed-period buying is the tiebreak toward neutral-positive.

The guide is the line that moves this and TTF ran 59/70/72 EUR/MWh through Q3 against 43-46 in Q2 and 31-35 a year earlier, after management had already put FY EBITDA at the low end of +5-8% with price rises back-loaded to H2 - and Viscofan cut its FY guide at Q3 2025 on the same mechanism, while the consensus is still 8 buy / 0 sell near EUR 70. Held small: the transmission is unquantified (hedging and cogeneration unmeasurable), Q3 is the first quarter with an FX tailwind, and ~2.3% disclosed short at ~16 days of volume is squeeze fuel against a negative.
